title: Setup code
description: The JSON inside a setup code, basalt-setup.1.<b64url(deflate-raw(json))>.<check> (CONTRACT.md, Setup from your laptop). basalt init --remote makes it on the bot's machine; basalt init --setup-code reads it on the person's own computer, and the connect service reads it from the connect page. Never the agent's password (its SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier instead, which is sensitive) and never anything of the admin. Closed: an unknown key is refused. Rules a schema cannot state (guard.from <= guard.to, and < for UPGRADE; at least one table in write or read, unless agent.allTables; a table in only one of write and read; the agent role <prefix>_agent_<name> at most 63 bytes; expiresAt no later than the setupId's UUIDv7 time plus 10 minutes; a code without target carries engine, and an AGENT code without target carries agent.verifier) are in CONTRACT.md. Golden fixtures: setup-code.fixtures.json.

install.description: INSTALL: the guard (migrations guard.from+1..guard.to), the agent role with its password set from the verifier, its grants, and a portal passkey when none is active. Without target, a connect-only code (it must carry engine); the database is the one the person pastes on the connect page.

agentChange.description: AGENT: an existing agent's tables, replaced by write and read (or agent.allTables) as given; with a verifier its password is rotated, without one it is kept. Also applies missing migrations up to guard.to and registers a portal passkey when none is active. Without target, a connect-only recovery code (it must carry engine and agent.verifier); the connect service rotates the password of an existing role, or creates the role as INSTALL does when it does not exist.

upgrade.description: UPGRADE: the missing migrations up to guard.to only. No agent part: the password, grants and policies are unchanged. Always carries target: its engine already has an address.

engine.description: Planned (M4.1, CONTRACT.md, The setup code and Direct transport). The engine's identity, which the person's computer records in basalt_meta with the address given as --engine-url, never in the code. Optional in a code with target; required in a code without one, whose engine collects the database's address from the connect service with a request signed by this key. A code with an engine key that is not an uncompressed P-256 point on the curve is INVALID.

publicKey.description: The engine's signing key: its 91-byte SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER (id-ecPublicKey, prime256v1, uncompressed point), base64url without padding.

format.description: Payload format. A decoder refuses any other value as a newer format (update basalt), not as a damaged code.

setupId.description: UUIDv7 made by basalt init --remote. Single use: recorded in basalt_meta.setups by the laptop's install transaction. Time-ordered, so a code older than the agent's latest recorded setup is refused.

target.description: The database the bot's engine connects to, from its password-less connection string. The laptop and the connect service compare it with the admin connection string by database identity and refuse a mismatch (CO-17). Absent in a connect-only code (INSTALL, or AGENT with a verifier, both with engine), which only the connect service runs; the laptop command refuses it (CONNECT_ONLY).

host.description: Host name or IP address, as in the bot's connection string.

supabaseRef.description: The Supabase project ref when the connection string names one: the pooler user postgres.<ref> or the direct host db.<ref>.supabase.co. Absent otherwise. With it, the project ref and database decide identity, so the pooler and the direct host of one project match.

guard.description: basalt_meta schema versions. from: the version the bot read with the agent credential, 0 when it could not read one. to: the version the bot's build installs.

build.description: The bot's basalt version, named when the laptop's binary is older than guard.to (update basalt on this computer to at least <build>).

table.description: schema.table of plain (unquoted, lowercase) identifiers; never a system schema or basalt_meta.

allTables.description: CONTRACT.md, The setup code. In place of write and read: the agent gets write access to every ordinary and partitioned table in these schemas that the admin role owns when the setup runs (read access only to one without a primary key). Tables made later are not covered. The connect page and the laptop command list the concrete tables before the person approves.

schemas.description: public only. Supabase's auth and storage schemas are never included.

verifier.description: The agent password's SCRAM-SHA-256 verifier (RFC 5802, RFC 7677), as Postgres stores it: SCRAM-SHA-256$4096:<salt>$<StoredKey>:<ServerKey>, standard base64, a 16-byte random salt and 4096 iterations. Sensitive: it is not the password, but with one observed SCRAM exchange of the role it lets its holder log in as the agent (CONTRACT.md, The setup code).

newAgent.description: The new agent: its tables in write and read, or agent.allTables in their place. Key order: name, write, read, allTables, verifier, statementTimeoutMs.

changedAgent.description: The changed agent: its tables in write and read, or agent.allTables in their place; a verifier when its password is rotated. Key order: name, write, read, allTables, verifier, statementTimeoutMs.

agentName.description: The agent's name (guard.Names); its role <prefix>_agent_<name> fits in 63 bytes.

expiresAt.description: RFC 3339 UTC, whole seconds: 10 minutes after basalt init --remote made the code (CO-13).
